name: Tactical helmet
description: A dark green composite combat helmet with a rail down each side and a mount on the brow for night-vision gear. It stops shell fragments and most pistol rounds.
notes: Standing on its rim, front on +z: a dark green full-cut shell 250 mm across and 150 mm tall on a black rubber edge, a small black night-vision bracket on the brow, a slim black rail curving along each side, a hook-and-loop patch following the crown's curve and another on the back, a black counterweight pouch under the back patch, and a webbing chin harness hanging from the rails' ends to a padded cup and buckle on the floor. Shell in `nylon-ranger-green` so the black fittings read against it. A hollow shell fills little of its box. Slot `head`. It hosts helmet add-ons through four `helmet` points: the brow bracket (front, where goggles and night-vision mounts go on this open-faced helmet), the left and right rails, and the back patch; reach follows the helmet convention, quickest at the front and slowest at the back. Protection is a guess for an aramid shell, above the riot helmet against piercing. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Rifle back scabbard
description: A long leather scabbard on two shoulder straps that carries a rifle or shotgun slung across the back, its stock up behind the shoulder.
notes: Lying on its side along x: a brown leather sheath 950 mm long, narrow at the closed muzzle end and widening to 130 mm at the mouth for the receiver, with black welts along both edges, a black toe and rim, a hood strap with a brass stud over the mouth, and two black collars whose straps are laid out flat beside it to a brass buckle. The straps spread on the floor add air to the box. It looks like the large back quiver, which takes `back`, so this does too. Its one pocket is a grid sized to one long gun, as the javelin bag's is; drawing over the shoulder is slow, so its handling is the longest in the batch. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Six-pistol baldric
description: A broad leather sash worn over one shoulder and across the chest, with six pistol holsters hanging from it so a loaded gun is always to hand.
notes: Laid flat: a black leather sash in a closed loop 1.6 m round and 70 mm wide with a brass buckle on one bend, and six red-brown holsters, each 200 mm long with a black rim, toe and thumb-break strap, three hanging from each run with their muzzles pointing out. The loop encloses floor. It is worn across the chest like the cloth bandolier, so it takes `vest`. Each holster is a pocket sized to one pistol; the three on the back run are slower to reach. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Belly band holster
description: A wide stretch band worn round the stomach under a shirt, with a pocket for a pistol and one for a spare magazine. Hard to draw from without practice.
notes: Laid flat: an off-white elastic band in a closed ring 1.1 m round and 100 mm wide, a charcoal pistol pocket 180 mm long with a black rim and thumb-break strap and a charcoal magazine sleeve sewn on one run, and a grey hook-and-loop tab on the other where it fastens. The ring encloses floor. Slot: it sits round the stomach under the shirt and is worn alongside a belt and a vest, so neither `waist`, `torso` nor `vest` fits; it names a new slot, `belly`. The awkward draw is the longest pistol handling in the batch. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Thigh concealment band
description: A stretch band worn round the upper thigh under trousers or a skirt, with a pocket for a very small pistol and two slim sleeves for a magazine and a knife.
notes: Laid flat: a tan elastic band in a closed ring 700 mm round and 90 mm wide, with a brown pocket 130 mm long for a small pistol, a slim magazine sleeve on one run and a flat slip pocket and a grey hook-and-loop tab on the other. The ring encloses floor. A leg band takes `thigh`, as the drop-leg holster does. The pistol pocket is sized to a compact pistol; the awkward draw is a long handling time. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Ankle holster
description: A small leather holster on a fleece-lined band that straps round the ankle, hiding a backup pistol under the trouser leg.
notes: Lying on its side as a short open cuff: a tan leather band 330 mm round and 70 mm wide with dark fleece lining showing at both edges and inside, and a brown holster 120 mm long riding on top, with a black rim, toe and thumb-break strap with a brass stud. The cuff's hollow fills its box. It is belted over the boot and takes `ankle`, as the ankle pouch does. Its pocket is sized to a compact pistol; bending to the ankle makes it the slowest draw in the batch. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.

name: Bow sling
description: A set of cotton straps with a sleeve and a cup that hold a bow across the back, out of the way but quick to pull free.
notes: Laid flat: an olive drab shoulder strap in a loop 1.6 m round and 40 mm wide with a khaki shoulder pad, a canvas sleeve 280 mm long with brown edging at one end for the lower limb, a shallow canvas cup at the other for the upper limb, and a brown cross strap between them with a steel buckle. The strap loop encloses floor. It looks like a sling pack; a bow carried across the back takes `back`, as the large quiver does. Its one pocket is a grid sized to one bow. The worn look is pending: no worn model is authored.
